cases.name: Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.
UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc.

profile_text.body:
Suno is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company operates an AI music generation platform at suno.com that the site describes as allowing users to create complete original songs, including vocals, lyrics, and full production, from a single text prompt in under a minute. The site positions Suno against other AI music tools by noting that most produce only short instrumental loops, whereas Suno generates full tracks across any genre. Free access is available, with paid tiers adding commercial use rights and higher output volumes. The Pro plan offers 500 songs per month and access to v5.5, described as Suno's best and most personalized AI music model, while the Premier plan offers 2,000 songs per month and includes Suno Studio, which the site describes as a first-of-its-kind web-based generative audio workstation combining traditional DAW functionality with AI-powered creation, along with a multitrack editor, MIDI export, and persona voices.

Suno faces substantial litigation. The most prominent case is UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc., filed in the District of Massachusetts, and additional suits have been brought in the same district by Rugnetta, Pilavian, Reyna, and S.A. Jamendo v. Suno Inc. Further cases appear in the Southern District of Texas (Gawronski v. Suno Inc.), the Southern District of New York (Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.), and the Northern District of Illinois (Woulard v. Suno, Inc.). The held facts record 72 instances of legal exposure associated with Massachusetts, reflecting the concentration of cases in that jurisdiction.
